ranked.headline: Structural constraints in spatial transcriptomics annotation, alignment, and deconvolution
ranked.summary: Constrained LLM annotation, weak supervision, and multi-slice alignment are now benchmarked against expert-labeled spatial datasets.

ranked.headline: Tumor-naive ctDNA quantification without matched tumor sequencing
ranked.summary: Matched tumor sequencing is often unavailable, so tumor-naive methods estimate plasma ctDNA directly, now benchmarked at scale with in silico samples.

ranked.headline: Structure predictors in the loop steer de novo protein and antibody binder design
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and two published papers pair structure prediction with sequence design for binders, antibodies and small-molecule-binding proteins.

ranked.headline: Biologically structured models predict cellular responses to unseen gene perturbations
ranked.summary: Recent perturbation models add biological structure, distributional alignment, and multimodal embeddings to prediction of responses to unseen perturbations.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks test whether reported model performance survives realistic perturbations
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks across single-cell, microbiome, and protein-ligand models test whether reported performance survives realistic conditions.

ranked.headline: Effective reduced descriptions of stochastic and heterogeneous biological systems
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published cancer model reduce stochastic and heterogeneous biology to tractable effective descriptions.

ranked.headline: Calibrating imputation and reference bias in spatial and single-cell inference
ranked.summary: Recent work tests inference validity for imputed spatial transcriptomes and incomplete single-cell reference matrices.

ranked.headline: ML ranks peptide, antibody, epitope and glycan binding before experimental testing
ranked.summary: Frozen ESM-2 embeddings and active learning target costly docking and mutational scans, while new benchmarks test whether these models generalize.

ranked.headline: Synaptic motifs, E/I balance and neuromodulation shape neural circuit model dynamics
ranked.summary: Current work pairs specific software frameworks and mechanistic circuit models with defined biological questions across spinal, cortical, and network scales.

ranked.headline: Ancestry and cell-type context sharpen regulatory variant and eQTL interpretation
ranked.summary: Multi-ancestry eQTL and polygenic score studies now test whether regulatory and risk predictions gain accuracy when conditioned on context.

ranked.headline: LLM agents orchestrate omics and imaging analyses, evaluated on verifiable benchmarks
ranked.summary: Agents now sequence spatial proteomics, transcriptomics, and single-cell workflows, with evaluation shifting to verifiable and published-study conditions.

ranked.headline: MD simulations expose transient Rac1 pockets and MSMP-stabilized active CCR2-G complexes
ranked.summary: Molecular dynamics now resolves transient surface pockets and ligand-stabilized states in Rac1 and CCR2 complexes.

ranked.headline: Computational and screening methods infer functional consequences of genetic variants
ranked.summary: Tiling CRISPR screens and network-aware statistics now resolve variant consequences at residue, gene, and transcript scales.

ranked.headline: Residue contact networks and transfer entropy map allosteric information flow in proteins
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a publication apply residue-network methods to allostery, linking structural contacts to variant pathogenicity.

ranked.headline: Automated tools for repeat-aware, reproducible DNA sequencing analysis and benchmarking
ranked.summary: Workflow-encoded tools now target repeat-rich regions, long-read alignments, and platform error profiling in DNA sequencing data.

ranked.headline: Structured latent encodings of imaging, omics and histology for biological prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published multi-omics VAE extend multimodal integration to volumetric microscopy, histology, and incomplete omics data.

ranked.headline: Biological sequence models augmented with retrieval, text, graph, and topological inputs
ranked.summary: Recent 2026 work pairs pretrained sequence-model embeddings with auxiliary context for interaction, localization, and splice-site prediction.

ranked.headline: Models increasingly treat RNA-level identity as an input for drug activity prediction
ranked.summary: Isoform identity and cross-target sequence transfer are being modeled explicitly as inputs for predicting drug and oligonucleotide activity.

ranked.headline: Reduced-resolution simulation and independent benchmarking of structure predictors
ranked.summary: Physics-based and coarse-grained models now reach flexible and disordered systems at scale, while AlphaFold3 is tested on post-cutoff complexes.

ranked.headline: Trait-linked gene content comparisons across bacterial and fungal genomes
ranked.summary: Group-wise pangenome and genome-content comparisons are now linking gene repertoires to clinically relevant traits in bacteria and fungi.

ranked.headline: External evidence informs variant prioritization for rare and birth defect diagnosis
ranked.summary: Rare disease and birth defect genomics need prioritization beyond single core models, and three recent items test evidence-augmented approaches.

ranked.headline: Vertex models link cell division, adhesion, and microtubules to tissue shape
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published model apply vertex-based mechanics to division-driven contacts, contact-mediated signaling, and plant growth anisotropy.

ranked.headline: Effect-size and Bayesian scoring reshape regulatory motif and co-methylation inference
ranked.summary: Recent work reframes regulatory inference around effect magnitude, Bayesian models and principled candidate definition across ChIP-seq, m6A and domain data.

ranked.headline: Flexibility-aware simulation and map alignment for protein-peptide structure modeling
ranked.summary: Open tools now pair coarse-grained flexibility simulation and deep-learning map alignment with MD-derived protein-peptide interface signatures.

ranked.headline: Prior knowledge constrains omics inference of signaling and drug effects
ranked.summary: Recent preprints build curated pathway topology or healthy immune reference frames into proteomic and transcriptomic inference workflows.

ranked.headline: Vertebrate genomes resolve haplotypes, regulatory elements and sex-linked variation
ranked.summary: Reference-quality vertebrate assemblies and haplotype-aware tools now enable finer dissection of regulatory and sex-linked variation.

ranked.headline: Models separate technical artifacts from biological variability in single-cell RNA data
ranked.summary: Recent models address dropout, sequencing depth, and non-UMI amplification artifacts that obscure cell-level expression and modification dynamics.

ranked.headline: Computational models forecast cell fate trajectories from single-cell and imaging data
ranked.summary: FateLimit defines a fate half-life quantifying when single-cell omics make cell fate predictable; LaVOUS models lineage-tree expression dynamics.

ranked.headline: Machine learning links sequence features to antigen specificity in antibodies and TCRs
ranked.summary: ML-compatible yeast Fab libraries and paired-chain TCR models now generate public antibody-antigen data alongside specificity predictions.

ranked.headline: Alignment-free and graph-based tools reframe microbial genome and metagenome analysis
ranked.summary: New preprints and a published pipeline extend alignment-free, graph-based and consensus annotation approaches to microbial sequence data.

ranked.headline: Sequence-based transformers and generative frameworks model mRNA translation and design
ranked.summary: Sequence-native transformers now predict translation efficiency and design 5' UTRs, extending expression modeling to post-transcriptional outputs.

ranked.headline: Long-read and deep learning tools map chromatin, enhancer RNA, and G-quadruplex variation
ranked.summary: Standardized epigenomic references and haplotype-resolved long-read methods now enable locus-level analysis of regulatory variation.

ranked.headline: Computational inference of chromatin architecture and cis-regulatory connectivity
ranked.summary: Automated and calibrated models now quantify chromatin looping, distance bias, and regulatory graphs from sequence and imaging data.

ranked.headline: Linker length, remodeling and phase separation shape chromatin and RNP condensate states
ranked.summary: Coarse-grained models now connect nucleosome spacing, remodeling and binding saturation to chromatin and RNP condensate conformations.

ranked.headline: Computational models dissect NORSE inflammation, Abeta-Tau patterns, and aging artifacts
ranked.summary: Quantitative models of disease biology are being scrutinized for whether their outputs reflect biology or the analytic procedure that produced them.

ranked.headline: Mechanistic models couple viral replication to innate sensing and transcription control
ranked.summary: Recent work couples viral replication, host innate sensing and polymerase dynamics in quantitative models of infection.

ranked.headline: Python tools automate microscopy-based quantification of biological structure across…
ranked.summary: Recent publications and a preprint describe Python-based tools that automate quantitative measurements for three distinct imaging applications.

ranked.headline: Population models quantify insect control effects on pollinators and vector-borne…
ranked.summary: Quantitative models now extrapolate insect-targeted intervention and exposure effects from lab data and field trials to landscape and population scales, with…

ranked.headline: Cell-state atlases now link spatial, developmental and genetic architecture
ranked.summary: Spatial and single-nucleus atlases now resolve cell states alongside genetic association signals across human and bovine tissues.

ranked.headline: Simulated evolutionary ground truth tests reconstruction of ancestors and intermediates
ranked.summary: Forward-evolution and epistatic-landscape simulations now provide ground-truth trajectories for testing ancestral and intermediate sequence inference.
